After I lost my husband, the parenting tips that I learnt were so helpful to me: I began breathing calmly whenever I was feeling so sad or angry, and my kids really felt the difference because I was learning to keep calm.

Naming our feelings and being open about how we are feeling has helped me feel closer to my child. Before, I felt like I was the only one who was going through these emotions, but now I know that my child is feeling the same things. We can talk about it and help each other. We don’t feel alone anymore.

SourceText: Here are some tips to help you and your family through times of grief:
text: Hapa kuna vidokezo vya kukusaidia wewe na familia yako wakati wa majonzi:

SourceText: ACCEPT
text: KUBALI

SourceText:
Losing someone we love can affect us for weeks, months or years. There’s no right way to feel, and no need to feel better quickly.

Your teen may feel sad, angry, confused, or unwell. They may have nightmares, pain, or school problems. Even if they seem happy, they might still feel sad. This is all normal.
text:
Kumpoteza mtu tunayempenda kunaweza kutuathiri kwa majuma, miezi au mwaka. Hakuna njia sahihi ya kujihisi na hakuna haja ya kujisikia vizuri haraka.

Kijana wako anaweza kuhisi huzuni, hasira, kuchanganyikiwa, au vibaya. Wanaweza kuwa na ndoto mbaya, maumivu, au matatizo ya shule. Hata kama wanaonekana kuwa na furaha, bado wanaweza kuwa na huzuni. Haya yote ni ya kawaida.

SourceText: 5 stages of grief
text: Hatua 5 za huzuni

SourceText:
Many people experience grief in the following 5 stages. Knowing this helps you to better support your teen and take care of yourself: 

1: 😟 Denial: “This isn’t really happening.”
2: 😡 Anger: “I’m mad.”
3: 🙏🏾 Bargaining: “I wish I could change it.”
4: 😣 Depression: “I feel really sad.”
5: 😔 Acceptance: “I’m okay now, even though it still hurts.”
text:
Watu wengi hupitia huzuni kwa hatua 5 zifuatazo. Kujua hili inakusaidia kujua namna bora ya kumsaidia kijana wako na kujijali mwenyewe:

1: 😟 Kukataa: "Hii haiwezi kutokea"
2: 😡 Hasira: "Nimekasirika sana"
3: 🙏🏾 Kujitetea: “Laiti ningekuwa na uwezo wa kubadilisha hali hii"
4: 😣 Msongo wa mawazo: "Nahisi huzuni sana"
5: 😔 Kukubali: "Niko sawa sasa, japokuwa bado moyo wangu unaumia".

SourceText: SAY GOODBYE
text: SEMA KWAHERI

SourceText:
Find a way to say goodbye that feels right for you and your family. Some people hold a ceremony or have a special meal to celebrate the person.

Ask your teen what they would want to do to say goodbye.
text:
Tafuta njia ya kusema kwaheri inayokufaa wewe na familia yako. Baadhi ya watu hufanya sherehe au huandaa chakula maalum ili kumsherehekea mtu huyo.

Muulize kijana wako angependa kufanya nini ili kusema kwaheri.

SourceText: TALK
text: ZUNGUMZA

SourceText:
Talking or writing about the person can help bring comfort. Gently share your memories—both the happy ones and the hard ones.

Teens may sometimes feel the death was their fault. Kindly remind them it was not. Let them know they can always talk to you about their feelings, and show them it’s okay by sharing yours too.
text:
Kuzungumza au kuandika juu ya mtu huyo kunaweza kuleta faraja. Washirikishe kumbukumbu zako kwa upole zile zote zenye furaha na zile ngumu.

Wakati fulani vijana wanaweza kuhisi kifo kilikuwa kosa lao. Tafadhali wakumbushe haikuwa hivyo. Wajulishe kuwa wanaweza kuzungumza nawe kila wakati kuhusu hisia zao, na uwaonyeshe kuwa ni sawa kwa kuwakushirikisha zako pia.

SourceText:

SourceText:
When I lost my mom, everything changed. I was so sad, but it felt like my dad couldn't understand. Our relationship suffered. We did our own things and we stopped talking to each other. But then something incredible happened.

My dad learnt all these things from the app about what to do when you lose someone. He asked me how I was doing and we started to talk again. He explained that he was sad too, and he even said he was sorry for not talking to me after my mom died. We can now see that it is hard for both of us, and we can help each other. He is supporting me and we are a lot closer.

Greetings, greetings everyone.

Today our topic is positive instructions.

It is important to give positive instructions to our children, because when we give them positive instructions they know and understand what we are expecting them to do and they do it the way we want them to do it.

So, at the end it keeps everyone happy.

When you give positive instructions, your teen is more likely to listen!

SourceText:
Before, I used to raise my teens the way I was raised: I would tell them “don’t do this, don’t do that.” We used to fight a lot, but things have really changed when I learnt about giving positive instructions.

Now I focus on the behaviour I want to see, and give clear and simple instructions to my teens. It took time to learn to say “please do this” instead of “don’t do this.”

My teens and even my husband tell me that they love this way of doing things, because now they know what needs to be done. My teen said one day “I really love this new mom,” and my own stress levels have come down a lot.

Sasa nimejikita katika tabia niliyotaka kuiona, na natoa maelekezo ya wazi na rahisi kwa watoto wangu. Ilinichukua muda kujifunza kusema, tafadhali fanya hiki badala ya usifanye hivi. 
Mtoto wangu pamoja na mme wangu wanasema wanapenda namna hii ya ufanyaji vitu kwasababu sasa wanajua ni kitu gani kinafanyika. Mtoto wangu siku moja alisema, nampenda sana mama huyu mpya na msongo wangu wa mawazo umepungua kwa kiasi kikubwa.

Today's topic is family budgeting.

It is important to create a budget, but it is even more important to create a budget involving the entire family.

SourceText:
My teens used to ask for many things and couldn’t understand when I said, “I don’t have money for that right now.” They would say, “But you have a job!”

One day I sat with them and showed them all our monthly costs and how much is left. After that, they understood. Now they even share ideas on how we can save for small goals, like new shoes or birthdays, and bigger things like school fees. For my older one, I also opened a savings account.

Budgeting together has made me realise that it’s not just earning money that is important but actually showing up as a father. This has made me feel less stressed and less alone with the money worries, because now we plan together as a family.

Na kuwekeza kwenye vitu vikubwa kama vile ada za shule. Vilevile nimefungua akaunti ya akiba kwa ajili ya kijana wangu mkubwa.

Kupanga bajeti pamoja kumenifanya nitambue kwamba siyo tu kutafuta pesa ndio jambo muhimu lakini pia kujionyesha kama baba. Hii imenifanya nijihisi mwenye mawazo kidogo, na siyo peke yangu mwenye hofu ya pesa, kwa sababu kwa sasa tunapanga pamoja kama familia.

SourceText:
**Step 1: THINK**
Think about what you spend money on each month.
text:
**Hatua ya 1: FIKIRI**
Fikiria juu ya kitu kinacho kugharimu pesa kila mwezi.

SourceText:
- Draw pictures of all the things that you and your family spend money on each month.
- Write next to each picture how much each thing costs each month (there is no need to share the numbers if you don’t want to).
- Add up how much money you have to spend each month.
text:
- Chora picha za vitu vyote ambavyo vinakugharimu wewe na familia yako kila mwezi.
- Andika karibu na kila picha ni kiasi gani kila kitu kinagharimu kila mwezi (hakuna haja ya kushirikisha namba ikiwa hutaki).
- Ongeza kiasi cha pesa unachopaswa kutumia kila mwezi.

SourceText:
**Step 2: CHOOSE**
Think about your needs and wants.
- WANT is something you can live without. 
- NEED is something you cannot live without.
text:
**Hatua ya 2: CHAGUA**
Fikiria juu ya mahitaji na matakwa yako.
- KUTAKA ni kitu ambacho unaweza kuishi bila kuwa nacho. 
- UHITAJI ni kitu ambacho huwezi kuishi bila kuwa nacho.

SourceText:
Look at your list of things you spend money on and choose:

- Which are NEEDS that you cannot live without? Why?
- Which are WANTS which are nice to have but not essential? Why?
- Which things could you try to spend less money on?
text:
Angalia kwenye orodha yako, vitu vinavyo kugharimu pesa alafu uchague:

- Je, ni MAHITAJI gani ambayo huwezi kuishi bila kuwa nayo? Kwa nini?
- Je, ni MATAMANIO yapi ambayo ni mazuri kuwa nayo lakini sio muhimu? Kwa nini?
- Ni mambo gani unaweza kujaribu kutumia pesa kidogo?

SourceText:
**Step 3: BUILD**
Make a budget!
text:
**Hatua ya 3: JENGA**
Tengeneza bajeti!

SourceText:
I used to ask my mom to buy me nice clothes all the time. Each time, she would say “I do not have money,” but I knew that she was getting money from my uncle. I did not understand why she refused to buy me clothes. I thought at some point “she does not love me.”

But one day, she called me to sit down with her and asked “what are the needs and wants in our house.” I started to list all my needs and wants. Then my mother helped me to also think about the family needs. Now I understand where our money is going, towards the things we need as a family.

From that day, I understand I cannot come in and ask any time. Now, when I want something, I wait till the month-end when we all discuss the budget together to see if it fits. We understand each other better now.

Lakini siku moja, aliniita niketi naye na kuniuliza “ni mahitaji gani na matakwa gani katika nyumba yetu.” Nilianza kuorodhesha mahitaji na matakwa yangu yote. Kisha mama yangu akanisaidia pia kufikiria kuhusu mahitaji ya familia. Sasa ninaelewa pesa zetu zinaenda wapi, kuelekea vitu tunavyohitaji kama familia.

SourceText: Here are some skills to help guide you in spending one-on-one time with your teen!

SourceText: Many short moments of connection each day or week help build trust and give you more chances to guide your teen than long, serious conversations.

SourceText:
Let your teen choose.

Tell your teen that you would like to spend some time with them and that they can choose what to do or talk about. They might think this is weird at first, but they will come to enjoy this time with you!
text:

Mwambie kijana wako kwamba ungependa kutumia muda pamoja naye na kwamba anaweza kuchagua cha kufanya au cha kuzungumzia. Mwanzoni, anaweza kuona kuwa hili ni jambo la ajabu, lakini baadaye atafurahia muda huu wa kuwa na wewe!

SourceText: More tips

SourceText: One-on-one time helps you understand your teen’s world better. Ask open questions like “What was the best part of your day?” or “Can you show me something you enjoy?”. This helps them feel seen and supported.
text: Wakati wa maongezi ya moja kwa moja hukusaidia kuelewa dunia ya vijana wako vizuri zaidi. Uliza maswali ya wazi kama "Ni sehemu ipi bora ya siku yako?" au "Unaweza kunionesha kitu unachokipenda?". Hii inawasaidia kujihisi kuonekana na kuungwa mkono.

SourceText: STAY

SourceText:
Focus on your teen.

Switch off the TV and put phones aside. Look at your teen. Nod or say “I see” to show that you are really paying attention. Accept what they say without judging them.

- Walk to the shops
- Play a game/sport
- Do a chore together
- Prepare dinner
- Eat breakfast/lunch/dinner
- Watch a TV show

**Remember to use your new skills:**
📅 **DAY**: try to do it every day,
⚽ **PLAY**: let your teen choose how to spend one-on-one time, and 
🎯 **STAY**: be focused on your teen!

SourceText:
When my mother asked to spend time with me, I thought “Maybe something is wrong, maybe she is sick.” But she said “No, I just want to spend time.” I was sceptical, but I accepted.

She asked me what I like doing. It was strange and I was not comfortable, because she never ever spent time with me on my own.

The more she kept on trying and we spent this time together, it felt really nice. She got to share her own childhood with me, things I never heard before. That helped me to also share what is going on in my life. We even talk about boyfriends and about problems I have. I know I can talk to my mother now.
text:
Mama yangu alipoomba kukaa nami, nilifikiri “Labda kuna tatizo, labda ni mgonjwa.” Lakini alisema, "Hapana, nataka tu kakaa nami." Nilikuwa na shaka, lakini nilikubali.

Aliniuliza ninapenda kufanya nini. Ilikuwa ya kushangaza na sikuwa na raha, kwa sababu hakuwahi kutumia wakati na mimi peke yangu.

Kadiri alivyozidi kujaribu na kuwa na wakati huu pamoja, nilijisikia vizuri sana. Alnishirikisha maisha yake ya utotoni, mambo ambayo sikuwahi kuyasikia hapo awali. Hilo lilinisaidia pia kushiriki kile kinachoendelea katika maisha yangu. Tunazungumza hata juu ya wapenzi na shida nilizonazo. Najua naweza kuzungumza na mama yangu sasa.

When we learnt about this praising thing I thought, “We were never praised for things as teenagers, so why should we start now?” But I got interested when I learnt what the benefits of praising could be.

Right after the weekly workshop, I noticed my teen doing what they do every day: washing the dishes. And I said “Thank you for washing the dishes, my girl, it really makes me happy that you are helping out.” My teen was smiling and she even came to give me a hug, which she never does.

This praising business is hard. I still forget sometimes or give praise at the same time as criticism. But praising really makes a difference. I never thought that a simple praise could make such a change in a person!

SourceText:
I was grateful when my mother learned about praise.

Before the workshop, she mostly noticed when I did something wrong. She would shout and sometimes hit me.

But after the workshop, she began praising me for small things — even things she never noticed before, like my good maths grades. At first I thought, ‘What is going on?’ But she kept doing it. I liked it, so I started doing more good things.

It feels good that my mother now sees the good in me, not only the bad.

One day during one-on-one time, I told her, ‘Thank you, Mama, for saying something nice when I do things well, not only when I do things wrong.’ It made both of us very happy.
text:

Kabla ya mafunzo, alipotambua nimefanya kosa, alikuwa anaweza kunifokea na mara nyingine kunipiga.

Lakini baada ya mafunzo, alianza kunipongeza hata kwa jambo dogo- hata mambo ambayo hakuwa ameyatambua kabla, mfano maksi nzuri za hesabu nilizozipata. mara ya kwanza nilijiuliza, nini kinaendelea? lakini aliendelea kufanya hivyo. Nilipenda na nilianza kufanya vitu vizuri zaidi.

Ni jambo jema kwamba kwa sasa mama yangu anayaona mema ndani yangu, na sio mabaya pekee

Siku moja tulipokuwa wawili, nilimwambia, ‘Asante mama, kwa kuniongelea vizuri ninapofanya vitu vizuri, na sio ninapokosea tu.’ Inatufanya wote kwa pamoja tuwe wenye furaha.

SourceText:
Greetings, everyone.

Today's topic is problem solving.

We all know that in life there are times where we face problems, and we all know in a way that when we find ourselves in these situations, it is difficult to think of immediate positive solutions.

Therefore, it is important that when we are facing problems we take a pause, we breathe, keep calm and think of problem-solving skills that we may use.

Remember to include our teenagers when we are solving problems. This will help them to become responsible and learn how to solve their own problems in the future.
text:
Habari zenu.

Maada ya leo inahusu utatuzi wa matatizo.

Sote tunajua kuwa katika maisha kuna nyakati tunakabiliwa na matatizo, na sote tunajua kwa namna fulani kwamba tunapojikuta katika nyakati hizo, ni vigumu kufikiria haraka ufumbuzi chanya.

Kwa hiyo, tunapokabiliwa na matatizo ni muhimu tupumzike, tupumuwe, tutulie na tufikirie ujuzi wa kutatua matatizo tunaoweza kutumia.

Tunapotatua matatizo tukumbuke kuwashirikisha vijana wetu. Kufanya hivyo kutawasaidia kuwajibika na kujifunza jinsi ya kutatua matatizo yao wenyewe siku zijazo.

SourceText:
As parents, we sometimes think we need to fix every problem by ourselves. And teens can think the same! 

By involving your teen, you strengthen your relationship as well as their confidence. Together you can overcome anything.

Kama wazazi, kuna muda tunafikiri kwamba tunahitaji kutatua matatizo wenyewe. Na vijana wanaweza kufikiri hivyo!

SourceText:
I did not have a good relationship with my daughter. I was always shouting at her, and she was refusing to go to school.

Only when I started spending One-on-One time with her did I realise she was being bullied at school. We sat down and used the steps of problem solving. We identified the problem and figured out solutions together: “What can I do as a parent so you can feel safe and attend school?”

We agreed I would talk to her teacher to find a way forward. We found the solutions together, and now we are much closer.
text:

Tulilitambua tatizo na kulipatia suluhisho kwa pamoja: "Nini nachoweza kukifanya kama mzazi ili ujihisi salama na uweze kuhudhulia shuleni?"

Tulikubaliana naweza kuzungumza na mwalimu wake ili kupata ufumbuzi zaidi. Tulipata suluhisho kwa pamoja na sasa tupo karibu zaidi.

SourceText:
When something bad happens, we often get upset and blame. But what our teens really need is someone to help find solutions together. 

Listen to them, accept how they see and feel things, and thank them for trusting you.

Teaching your teen how to deal with problems will help them for the rest of their lives. What a gift!
text:
Jambo baya linapojitokeza, mara nyingi huwa tunakasirika au kulaumu. Lakini kile vijana wetu wanahitaji ni mtu wa kuwasaidia kutafuta utatuzi pamoja.

Wasikilize, kubaliana na namna wanavyo ona na kuhisi vitu, na washukuru kwa kukuamini.

Kuwafundisha vijana wako namna ya kushughulikia matatizo itawasaidia wao maisha yao yote. Ni zawadi ya kipekee!

SourceText:
**Here are some examples of problems other parents solved with their teens:**

- My teenager does not want to go to school
- I am worried my teenager will get pregnant or will get someone pregnant
- I am worried about what my teen does online
- My teenager is hanging out with bad friends
- My teenager is lazy
- My teenager is not doing their school work
- My teenager might be using drugs

- Kijana wangu ana barizi marafiki wabaya
- Kijana wangu ni mvivu

SourceText: Can you make an impact on your community with these skills? Hear @data.characters.media_son_2.name's story

SourceText:
When my father introduced the problem-solving steps to me, it helped me with my family, but it also helped me with my friends.

I told my friends about the steps, and now when we are arguing we sit down and everyone comes up with solutions. We then look for the negatives and positives of each solution, and we agree “okay let’s try this one.”

My friends even took it to their own homes, and it is helping with their families as well!

It is great when others listen to you and accept your ideas even though you are young. We can all bring that harmony with our friends and family.
text:
Pindi baba yangu aliponitambulisha hatua za kutatua tatizo, ilinisaidia mimi, familia yangu lakini pia iliwasaidia marafiki zangu.

Niliwaambia marafiki zangu kuhusu hatua hizo, na sasa wakati tunapobishana, tunakaa chini na kila mmoja anakuja na suluhisho. Kisha tunaangalia madhara hasi na chanya ya kila suluhisho na tunakubaliana ''sawa ngoja tujaribu hii moja.''

Marafiki zangu huchukuwa na kupeleka nyumbani kwao, na inawasaidia wao na familia zao pia!

Ni furaha pindi ambapo wengine wanakusikiliza na kukubaliana na mawazo yako hata kama wewe ni mdogo. Sote tunaweza kuleta maelewano na marafiki na familia.

Greetings, everyone.

Today our topic is teen safety.

It is our responsibility as parents to keep our teens safe at all times. We need to ensure that our teenagers are safe in the communities that we live in. It is our responsibility that we make them aware of the safe and unsafe areas in the communities.

It is also our responsibility to ensure that they understand the dangers that they might be exposed to when they are online. That way our teenagers will be responsible and be able to make right decisions to keep themselves safe too.

Habari zenu?

Leo mada yetu inahusu usalama wa vijana.

Kama wazazi, ni jukumu letu kuwaweka salama vijana wetu wakati wote. Tunahitaji kuhakikisha kuwa vijana wetu wako salama katika jamii tunazoishi. Ni jukumu letu kuwafahamisha maeneo salama na yasiyo salama katika jamii hizo.

Pia ni jukumu letu kuhakikisha kwamba wanaelewa hatari zinazoweza kuwakabili wanapokuwa mtandaoni. Kwa njia hiyo, vijana wetu pia watawajibika na wataweza kufanya maamuzi sahihi ya kujiweka salama.

Zungumzia pia jinsi jambo fulani linapowekwa mtandaoni, linabaki pale daima. Wanaweza kujua mfano kutoka kwa marafiki zao.

SourceText: RULES
text: SHERIA

SourceText: Make rules with your teen about how they can stay safe in your community (especially in risky areas that cannot be avoided), and how they can safely use the apps and websites that they like.
text: Tengeneza sheria na kijana wako kuhusu jinsi ya kujilinda katika jamii yenu (hasa katika maeneo hatari ambayo hayaepukiki), na jinsi wanavyoweza kutumia kwa usalama programu na tovuti wanazozipenda.

SourceText: Explore with your teen if you can create a rule around sharing with a trusted adult when something feels wrong. This can really help them stay safe in person and online.
text: Chunguza pamoja na kijana wako kama mnaweza kuunda sheria kuhusu kushirikisha jambo kwa mtu mzima anayeaminika wakati unapo hisi jambo linakuwa si sawa. Hii inaweza kuwasaidia sana kubaki salama, kihalisi na mtandaoni.

SourceText: SAFETY WORD
text: NENO LA USALAMA

SourceText: Agree on a Safety Word. If something happens that makes your teen upset, uncomfortable or scared, they can say the Safety Word and you will help them without getting angry or punishing them, even if they were doing something wrong.
text: Kukubaliana juu ya Neno la Usalama. Ikiwa kutatokea jambo lolote litakalomfanya kijana wako kuhisi huzuni, wasiwasi au hofu, anaweza kusema Neno la Usalama na utamsaidia bila kuchukizwa au kumwadhibu, hata kama alikuwa anafanya kitu kisicho sahihi.

SourceText:
When my friends or I got into trouble, I would always try to hide it from my mother because she would get so angry and shout at me.

When we made the map of safe and unsafe places, I learnt a lot – also why it is dangerous to share every picture online. My mother told me I can always ask her if there is a problem and she promised she would not get mad.

She kept her promise, so now if I have a problem or I do not feel safe I know we can always come up with a solution together. I can even talk to my mother about the things I do online now!

Aliweka ahadi yake, hivyo sasa nikiwa na tatizo au nikihisi kutokuwa salama, najua tunaweza kutafuta suluhisho pamoja. Hata pia ninaweza kuzungumza na mama yangu kuhusu mambo ninayofanya mtandaoni sasa!

SourceText:
Greetings, everyone.

Today's topic is self-care.

There are times when we experience challenges, face problems and do not know what to do. It is important to take care of ourselves to learn the techniques for keeping ourselves calm, in case problems, challenges or issues come up.

When we are calm we are in a good state to think positively and come up with positive solutions to any challenges we may be facing.
text:
Habari zenu?

Mada ya leo inahusu kujithamini wenyewe.

Kuna nyakati tunapata changamoto, tunakabiliwa na matatizo na hatujui cha kufanya. Ni muhimu kujithamini kwa kujifunza mbinu tunazoweza kuzitumia kuwa watulivu iwapo matatizo, changamoto au shida zitatokea.

Tunapokuwa watulivu, tunakuwa katika hali nzuri ya kufikiria vizuri na kupata ufumbuzi chanya wa changamoto zozote tunazoweza kukabiliwa nazo.

SourceText:
Why self-care?

We often don’t look after ourselves enough. But this is so important, especially as a parent!

Reducing our stress and treating ourselves well helps us AND our teenagers.
text:
Kwa nini kujitunza?

Mara nyingi hatujali vya kutosha kuhusu sisi wenyewe. Lakini hili ni jambo la muhimu sana, hasa kama mzazi!

Kupunguza msongo wa mawazo na kujitendea vema kunatusaidia sisi pamoja na vijana wetu pia.

For me as a parent, it was almost impossible to find time for myself. I was always busy taking care of everyone else. Through @global.app_name, I realised how important it is to take care of myself. It helps me AND my family!

Having a moment for myself helps me to breathe and notice how I feel. Even 5 minutes to have a cup of tea makes a big difference. Now I can deal with my stress better.

Kupata muda kidogo kwa ajili yangu hunisaidia kupumua na kutambua jinsi ninavyohisi.hata dakika 5 za kunywa chai hufanya tofauti kubwa. Sasa ninaweza kukabiliana na msongo wa mawazo vyema.

Take a moment now to relax. Breathe in slowly as you count to three... and breathe out as you count to three. Feel your body relax with each breath. 

Try this whenever you are feeling stressed and need a break. A few calm breaths can make a big difference.

SourceText:
This module includes content that may be sensitive. You can check it out by yourself first. This will prepare you well for sharing the content with your teen and others afterwards.

If you need support, see the “Support Contacts” section in your Library for help.

SourceText:
Today’s topic is body changes and intimate relationships.

Teens go through many changes in their bodies and feelings. Talking to them helps them handle it better.

Let your teen know you’re there to listen and support them. You don’t need all the answers—just being there helps them feel safe and make good choices.
text:
Mada ya leo inahusu mabadiliko ya mwili na mahusiano ya kimapenzi.

Vijana hupitia mabadiliko mengi katika miili yao na hisia. Kwa kuzungumza nao unaweza kuwasaidia kushughulikia mabadiliko haya pia.

Mwambie kijana wako kwamba upo kumsikiliza na kumpa msaada. Hauhitaji kujibu maswali yote — uwepo wako unasaidia ajisikie salama na kufanya machaguo mazuri.

SourceText:
**Think back to your own teenage years:**

- Did you face any challenges with body changes or relationships?
- What support or advice do you wish you had?
- Do you think your teen might be going through something similar?
text:
**Fikiria miaka yako ya ujana:**

- Je, umewahi kupata changamoto kutokana na mabadiliko ya mwili au mahusiano?
- Je ni aina gani ya msaada au ushauri unatamani ungepata?
- Je, unafikiri kijana wako anaweza kuwa anapitia jambo linalofanana?

SourceText: Why talk with your teen about body changes and relationships? Tap play to find out
text: Kwanini unazungumza na kijana wako kuhusu mabadiliko ya mwili na mahusiano? Bofya kucheza na utambue

SourceText:
Greetings, everyone.

Today's topic is body changes and intimate relationships.

Discussing body and intimate relationships with your child can be difficult. However, it is important to have these discussions in order for your teen to understand that this stage of life is normal. This will help them to acknowledge the changes in their bodies and be able to make positive decisions regarding intimate relationships.
text:
Habari zenu.

Mada ya leo ni mabadiliko ya mwili na mahusiano ya kimapenzi.

Kujadili mabadiliko ya mwili na mahusiano ya kimapenzi na mtoto wako inaweza kuwa ngumu. Hata hivyo, ni muhimu kuwa na majadiliano haya ili kijana wako aelewe kwamba hatua hii ya maisha ni ya kawaida. Hii itawasaidia kutambua mabadiliko katika miili yao na kuwa na uwezo wa kufanya maamuzi chanya kuhusu mahusiano ya kimapenzi.

SourceText: Even if these conversations feel uncomfortable at first, starting small can build trust. You might be surprised by how much your teen wants to share once they know you are ready to listen without judgment.

Thanks to the app, I can now talk to my son about all these changes that he is going through with his body and emotions and relationships. We were both not comfortable bringing it up before, but the practical examples in the app made it possible for us to start talking. And I was really surprised by how many questions and experiences my son already has, even though he is only 14!

Now he can come to me if there is something happening at school or if he is not sure how to handle something. The other day he even told me that some of his friends were making fun of him because he does not have a girlfriend yet, so we talked about it and I could explain to him that it is important to focus on school first and that it is never okay for someone to pressure him to have a relationship.

Hii pia itawasaidia kukabiliana vyema na hisia za kingono kwa usalama.

SourceText:
It’s good to start talking about body changes and relationships early - by gently answering your child’s questions.

You don’t need to explain everything. Just give simple, honest answers that match their age and understanding.

Ni vizuri kuanza kuzungumzia kuhusu mabadiliko ya kimwili na mahusiano mapema-kwa kujibu kwa utulivu maswali ya kijana wako.

SourceText:
This may not work.

When we try to control too much, both girls and boys may do the opposite of what we want.

But when we guide them and give them space to make choices, they often act more responsibly.

This may not work. 

Both boys and girls get pressure and information from many places we can’t control.

As parents, we can guide and prepare them to know what is right or wrong—and help them feel confident to make good decisions.
text:
Hii inaweza hisifanye kazi.

Vijana wakiume na wakike wote kwa pamoja wanapata taharifa kutoka sehemu mbalimbali ambazo hatuwezi kudhibiti.

Kama wazazi, tunaweza waongoza na kuwaandaa wao kufahamu kipi ni sahihi na kipi sio sahihi na kuwafanya kujihisi huru kufanya maamuzi.

SourceText:
That’s right.

When your teen feels trusted, they are more likely to trust you and come to you for advice or help.

Praise and thank them when they share. Avoid judging, so they feel safe to talk to you again.
text:
Hiyo ni kweli.

Mpongeze na mshukuru anapokushirkisha. Epuka kumhukumu, ili ahisi salama kuzungumza nawewe tena.

SourceText:
That’s right.

Good decisions come from thinking through the consequences. Talk openly with your teen when there’s a problem. Listen to each other and find solutions together.

Each challenge is an opportunity to teach your teen that actions have consequences—and you can handle them as a team.

Remember to praise each other for working through tough situations together.
text:

Maamuzi mazuri hutokea kwa kufikiria matokeo. Zungumza kwa uwazi na kijana wako pale mnapokumbana na tatizo. Sikilizaneni ninyi kwa ninyi na tafuteni suluhisho pamoja.

Kila changamoto ni nafasi ya kumfundisha kijana wako kwamba matendo yana matokeo—na kwamba mnaweza kuyakabili kwa pamoja kama timu.

Kumbuka kupongezana kwa kushirikiana kwa kupitia hali ngumu pamoja.

SourceText:
That’s right.

To stay safe, both boys and girls need to know the difference between respectful behaviours and relationships, and unhealthy ones..

Respectful relationships feel caring, safe, and fair. Unhealthy ones involve pressure, discomfort, or feeling unsafe.

No one should be forced to do something they’re not okay with.
text:

Kuwa salama, vijana wa kike na wakiume wote kwa pamoja wanahitaji kufahamu tofauti kati ya tabia njema, mahusiano na na yale yasio na afya.

Mahusiano ya kuheshimiana yanakufanya ujihisi salama, naya haki. Yasiyokuwa na afya yanahusisha msongo wa mawazo, wasiwasi na kutojihisi salama.

Hakuna anaeweza kulazimishwa kufanya kitu ambacho anahisi sio saw kukifanya.

SourceText:

Teens hear many things about sex—from school, friends, or social media. Some of it is wrong.

Knowing about sex doesn’t mean they are having sex. Good information helps them stay safe and understand why waiting to have sex can be a good choice.

Without this knowledge, they may face problems, like not knowing how pregnancy happens or the risks of sex.
text:
Hiyo sio sahihi kabisa.

Vijana husikia mambo mengi kuhusu ngono—kutoka shuleni, kwa marafiki, au kwenye mitandao ya kijamii. Baadhi ya taarifa hizo si sahihi.

Kujua kuhusu ngono haimaanishi kwamba wanafanya ngono. Taarifa sahihi huwasaidia kuwa salama na kuelewa kwa nini kusubiri kabla ya kufanya ngono kunaweza kuwa uamuzi mzuri.

bila maarifa, wanaweza kukumbana na matatizo, kama kutokujua kwa namna gani mimba inatokea au hatari vya ngono.

SourceText:
That’s not quite right.

Your teen might have a boyfriend or girlfriend and not tell you.

If you make them hide it, they may not come to you with questions or problems—and this can lead to risky situations.
text:
Hiyo si sahihi kabisa.

Kijana wako anaweza kuwa na mpenzi na asiwe amekuambia.

Kama ukiwalazimisha kuficha uhusiano huo, wanaweza wasikushirikishe maswali au matatizo yao—na hili linaweza kuwapelekea kwenye hali za hatari.

SourceText:
That’s right.

Teens are figuring out who they are. They look to friends and media for answers, and may feel pressure to do things they’re not ready for.

Talk calmly with your teen about waiting to have sex until they feel ready, are in a safe relationship, and understand the consequences. Focus on guiding them calmly to make healthy choices.
text:
Hiyo ni sawa.

Zungumza kwa utulivu na kijana wako kuhusu kusubiri kufanya ngono hadi pale atakapojihisi yuko tayari, yuko kwenye uhusiano salama, na anaelewa matokeo ya maamuzi yake. Lenga kuwaongoza kwa utulivu ili wafanye maamuzi yenye afya.

You can always ask trusted adults or your local clinic for more information, and your teen can too.

How can I support my teen with body changes, relationships, and staying safe?

Try selecting each option to learn more!

Jaribu kuchagua kila chaguo ili kujifunza zaidi!

SourceText: Talk about body changes and puberty
text: Zungumzia mabadiliko ya mwili na balehe

SourceText: Talk with your teen about normal body changes like growing taller, more body hair, voice changes, breasts or periods, and stronger emotions or liking someone. Explain that everyone grows at their own pace. Encourage them to ask you or another trusted adult any questions.
text: Zungumza na vijana wako kuhusiana na mabadiliko yakawaida ya mwili kama kuongezeka kimo, kuota nywele sehemu za siri, na mabadiliko ya sauti, maziwa au siku zao, na kuwa hisia kali au kuanza kumpenda mtu kimapenzi. Waeleze kuwa kila mmoja hukua kwa namna yake. Wasisitize kuuliza swali lolote kwako au mtu mzima anaeaminika.

SourceText: Discuss risks and protection
text: Jadili hatari na usalama

SourceText: Help your teen understand how pregnancy happens and how infections like HIV and chlamydia can spread through sex. Explain that condoms help protect against infections and pregnancy. Early pregnancy can affect their health, school and future plans. If your teen gets pregnant, support them and make sure they get the help they need.
text: Msaidie kijana wako kutambua ni kwa namna gani mimba hupatikana na kwa namna gani magonjwa ya kuambukiza kama VVU na Klamidia yanavyoweza kusambaa kwa njia ya ngono. Waeleze kwamba kondomu inaweza kusaidia kuwakinga dhidi ya mimba au magonjwa ya kuambukizwa. Mimba za utotoni zinaweza kuathiri afya zao, shule na malengo yao ya badae. Kama kijana wako akipata ujauzito, wasaidie na uhakikishe wanapata msaada wanao hitaji.

SourceText: How to say 'no'
text: Namna ya kusema 'Hapana'

SourceText: Make sure that your teen knows that others should always treat them with respect and kindness, and they should do the same. In relationships, both people need to feel safe and say yes without pressure. This is called ‘consent’. Teens can say ‘no’ at any time.
text: Hakikisha kuwa vijana wako wanafahamu kuwa wanatakiwa kuwatendea kwa heshima na kwa wema, na wao wanatakiwa kutenda hivo pia. Kwenye mahusiano watu wote wanatakiwa kujihisi salama na kusema ndio bila kuhofia. Hii inaitwa 'ridhaa'. Vijana wanaweza sema hapana muda wowote.

SourceText: Know where to go for help
text: Jua mahali pakwenda kupata msaada

SourceText:
You and your teen can get support from trusted adults, school counsellors, and clinics for questions about body changes, relationships, safety, or ways to prevent pregnancy and infections. 

Talk with your teen about who they can go to if they feel unsure or unsafe.
text: Wewe na kijana wako mnaweza kupata msaada kutoka kwa watu wazima wanaoaminika, washauri wa shuleni, na kliniki kwa ajili ya maswali yanayohusu mabadiliko ya mwili, mahusiano, usalama, au njia za kuzuia mimba na maambukizi.

SourceText:
Discussing body changes and intimate relationships can be uncomfortable, but it is so important in order to keep your teen happy, healthy and safe. 

Here are some skills to help you get started.
text:
Kujadili kuhusu mabadiliko ya mwili na mahusiano ya kimapenzi kunaweza kuwa kwa hali ya kutokuwa na raha, lakini ni muhimu sana ili kuhakikisha kijana wako anakuwa mwenye furaha, afya njema, na salama.

Hapa kuna baadhi ya ujuzi wa kukusaidia kuanza mazungumzo hayo.

SourceText: BUILD
text: KUJENGA

SourceText:
Build a strong relationship with your teen by spending time with them and showing them you trust them. Create a safe, encouraging space, and avoid judging them.

That will make your teen share their questions and worries with you, when they need advice or are in a potentially dangerous situation.
text:
Jenga uhusiano mzuri na kijana wako kwa kutumia muda pamoja naye na kumuonyesha kuwa unamwamini. Unda nafasi salama, ya kutia moyo, na uepuke kumuhukumu.

Hilo litamfanya kijana wako akushirikishe anapokuwa na maswali na wasiwasi, anapohitaji ushauri au yuko katika hali ya hatari.

SourceText: START
text: ANZA

SourceText:
Your teen may feel shy or scared, so parents need to start the talk about body changes and intimate relationships.

Begin early by answering questions simply and honestly. This builds confidence for you and your child.

It’s okay to feel uncomfortable. Be open, use the correct words, and get help if you don’t know all the answers.
text:
Kijana wako anaweza kuhisi aibu au hofu, hivyo ni jukumu la mzazi kuanzisha mazungumzo kuhusu mabadiliko ya mwili na mahusiano ya kimapenzi.

Anza mapema kwa kujibu maswali kwa urahisi na kwa uaminifu. Hii hujenga kujiamini kwako na kwa mtoto wako.

Ni sawa kuhisi kutokuwa na raha. Kuwa wazi, tumia maneno sahihi, na tafuta msaada kama hujui majibu yote.

SourceText: GUIDE
text: MWONGOZO

SourceText:
Your teen will hear about sex from many places. If they feel safe with you, you can help them find good information and make smart choices.

Help them think about consequences without shame or blame. Make sure they know they should never feel pressure (or pressure others) into sex or a relationship.

You can also ask other adults or health workers for help and information.

Wasaidie kufikiria kuhusu matokeo ya maamuzi yao bila aibu wala lawama. Hakikisha anajua kuwa hapaswi kulazimishwa (wala kumlazimisha mtu mwingine) kuingia kwenye ngono au uhusiano.

Unaweza pia kuomba msaada na taarifa kutoka kwa watu wazima wengine au wahudumu wa afya.

SourceText: Learn how to protect yourself by knowing weak spots on an attacker’s body:

SourceText:

- Punch the attacker’s nose with your fist or the back of your elbow.
**EARS**
- With flat hands, smack the attacker’s ears from both sides as hard as possible. You can also pull or twist them.
**RIBS**
- Punch the attacker in the ribs with your fist or the back of your elbow.
**FINGERS**
- Pull the attacker's pinky or little finger away from the other fingers hard and fast (it breaks easily).
**SHINS**
- Kick against the attacker’s shins as hard as you can.
**TOP OF FEET**
- Lift your foot and stomp your heel on the top of your attacker’s foot.
text:
**KICHWA**
- Mpige kichwa cha mvamizi wako kwa ngumi, teke au kiwiko cha mkono wako.
**PUA**
- Mpige pua ya mvamizi wako kwa ngumi, teke au kiwiko cha mkono wako.
**MASIKIO**
- Kwa kutumia viganja vya mikono yako, mpige mvamizi wako kwenye masikio pande zote mbili kwa nguvu kadri uwezavyo. Unaweza pia kuyavuta au kuyatikisa.
**MBAVU**
- Mpige mbavu za mvamizi wako kwa kutumia ngumi, teke au kiwiko cha mkono wako.
**VIDOLE**
- Vuta kidole kidogo cha mvamizi wako mbali na vidole vingine kwa nguvu na haraka (kinavunjika kwa urahisi).
**KIDEVU**
- Mpige kidevu cha mvamizi wako kwa nguvu uwezavyo.

SourceText: Here are some skills to help you and your teen stay safe!
text: Hizi hapa ni baadhi ya mbinu zitakazomsaidia kijana wako kukaa salama!

SourceText: KNOW IT
text: FAHAMU

SourceText:
Know the difference between healthy and unhealthy relationships. If someone hurts you, it is never your fault.

You are allowed to say and do what is needed to stay safe and get away—don’t worry about what others think.

You are worth defending. You are strong and powerful.
text:
Fahamu tofauti kati ya mahusiano yenye afya na yasiyo na afya. Ukishashambuliwa ujue kuwa sio kosa lako kamwe. 

Unaruhusiwa kusema na kufanya kile kinachohitajika ili kuwa salama na kuondoka—usijali kuhusu kile ambacho wengine wanaweza kufikiria.

Unastahili kujitetea. Una uwezo na nguvu.

SourceText: SEE IT
text: ONA

SourceText:
If someone says or does something that makes you feel uncomfortable, it’s not okay. We all have the right to feel safe, especially at home.

See the warning signs and trust your feelings. If you feel unsafe, the goal is to get away.
text:
Kama mtu amaesema au kufanya kitu ambacho kitakufanya ujisikia kuwa na wasiwasi, sio sawa. Wote tuna haki ya kujisikia salama, hasa tukiwa nyumbani.

Angalia ishara hatarishi na uziamini hisia zako. Kama uhahisi kuwa na wasiwasi, lengo ni kuondoka.

SourceText: SAY IT
text: SEMA

SourceText:
Your voice can help stop an attack. Yell, call for help, warn, act, or use humour to stay safe.

Be clear, confident, and direct—use your words, body, and eyes.
text:
Sauti yako inaweza kukusaiudia kuzuia mashambulizi. Piga kelele, ita msaada, toa vitisho, igiza au kuwa mcheshi ili ukae salama.

Kuwa wazi, jiamini katika kutumia maneno yako, mwili na macho.

SourceText: DO IT
text: IFANYE

SourceText:
If your voice doesn’t help, use your body.

Know the strong parts of your body you can use, and where on the attacker’s body you can hit to stop them. Use what you can to protect yourself and get away.
text:
Kama sauti yako haitakusaidia, tumia mwili wako.

Tambua sehemu ya mwili wako ambayo ni imara unaweza kuitumia, na ni wapi kwenye mwili wa mvamizi unaweza ukampiga ili kumzuia. Tumia kinachowekana ili kijilinda mwenyewe na uondoke.

SourceText: More tips
text: Vidokezo zaidi

SourceText:
In danger, it’s normal to freeze or feel unsure. These tools can help you and your teen stay safe.

If you or your teen are hurt, it is never your fault. Talk to someone you trust.

As a parent, let your teen know they can always tell you anything, and you’ll find a solution together.
text:

Kama mzazi, mwache kijana wako ajue kwamba anaweza kukuambia kitu chochote, na mnaweza kutafuta suluhisho pamoja.

SourceText: Remember, when we practice responding calmly and sharing how we feel, our teens learn to do the same. This skill will help them their whole life!
text: Kumbuka, tunapojizoesha kujibu kwa utulivu na kushirikishana jinsi tunavyohisi, vijana wetu hujifunza kufanya vivyo hivyo. Ustadi huu utawasaidia maisha yao yote!

SourceText: Hear how @data.characters.media_son_1.name learned to stay calm from his father
text: Sikia jinsi @data.characters.media_son_1.name alivyojifunza kuwa mtulivu kutoka kwa baba yake
note: The string @data.characters.media_son_1.name should not be translated.

SourceText:
Whenever I would do something wrong, my father would get so angry at me and beat me. He would not even listen to me and I would get so angry as well at him and everyone else.

Now, when he gets angry, he first takes a few deep breaths before he responds. It makes everyone calm down instead of causing a big fight.

It really helped me at home and at school, because even me I am no longer slashing everyone and I am no longer this moody person. When I feel really angry or stressed, I also take deep breaths like my father does. I am a different person.
text:
Pindi nilipofanya kitu kibaya, Baba yangu alinikasirikia sana na kunipiga. Alikuwa hanisikilizi na hii ilinifanya kumkasirikia yeye pamoja na watu wengine.

Sasa, pindi anapokuwa na hasira, anachukua dakika chache kuvuta pumzi ndefu kabla hajajibu chochote. Inafanya kila mtu kutulia badala ya kusababisha ugomvi mkubwa.

Hii inanisaidia sana nyumbani na hata shuleni, hata Mimi sasa siwakasirikii wengine na si mtu wa hisia kali. Pindi ninapojihisi hasira au mwenye msongo wa mawazo, Navuta pumzi ndefu kama Baba yangu anavyofanya. Nimekuwa mtu tofauti.

SourceText: Power of three
text: Nguvu ya tatu

SourceText:
Close your eyes.
Let's use the magic power of 3 to stay present and relax. 

Name 3 sounds you can hear right now.
Name 3 smells you can smell right now.
Name your 3 favourite foods.
What are 3 things you can be grateful for right now.

At the end of a touch day, thinking of 3 things to be grateful for can help us find the courage to try again tomorrow.
text:

Hebu tutumie maajabu ya namba 3 ili tuendelee kuwepo na kupumzika.

Taja harufu 3 unaweza kunusa sasa hivi.
Taja vyakula 3 unavyovipenda.

You are a star!

Shusha pumzi kwa kuhesabu mara tatu. 1, 2, 3.

SourceText:

Take a minute to think about the day.

Think about one positive or fun thing you did.
Praise yourself for one thing you did well today. 
Think of one thing you can do differently tomorrow.  
Think of one thing that you are grateful for.
text:

Fikiria jambo moja chanya au la kufurahisha ulilolifanya.

Fikiria jambo moja unaloweza kulifanya tofauti kesho. 
Fikiria jambo moja unalolishukuru.

SourceText: Pause to respond
text: Simamisha ili ujibu

SourceText:
Close your eyes. 

Do your children ever make you feel like screaming? 

Give yourself a 10-second pause. Breathe in and out slowly 5 times. 

Then try responding in a calmer way.

Millions of parents say this helps – A LOT.
text:
Fumba macho yako.

Je, watoto wako huwa wanakufanya utake kufoka?

Jipumzishe kwa sekunde 10. Vuta pumzi ndani na nje taratibu mara 5.

Kisha jaribu kujibu kwa utulivu zaidi.

Mamilioni ya wazazi wanasema hii inasaidia - SANA.

SourceText: Small things
text: Vitu vidogo

SourceText:
Close your eyes.  

Take a moment to stop what you are doing and connect with your breath.   

What is one thing you can be grateful for right now?  
What is one thing that brings you happiness?  
What is one thing that you love?  

They do not have to be big. Sometimes the small things in life count the most!
text:
Fumba macho yako.

Acha kwa muda kile unachokifanya ili uhusiane na pumzi yako.

Je, ni jambo gani moja unalolishukuru sasa hivi?
Je, ni jambo gani moja linalokuletea furaha?
Je, ni jambo gani moja unalolipenda?

Si lazima yawe makubwa. Wakati mwingine mambo madogo maishani ndiyo muhimu zaidi!

SourceText: Body scan
text: Uchunguzi wa mwili

SourceText:
Here is an activity to relax your body: 

Sit comfortably and close your eyes if you can. 
Imagine a golden ring scanning your body from your feet to your head.  
Pay attention as it moves up and down your body. Are there any areas that feel tense? Numb? Painful?  
Focus on those areas for a moment. Breathe into the area and, when you breathe out, try to let go of any tension or pain.  
Do this for a few breaths.  

Open your eyes. How does your body feel now?

You can also try this next time you find yourself lying in bed unable to sleep!
text:
Hapa kuna shughuli ya kupumzisha mwili wako:

Keti kwa raha mstarehe halafu ufumbe macho yako ukiweza.
Fikiria kama kuna pete ya dhahabu inauchunguza mwili wako kuanzia unyayoni hadi utosini.
Sikiliza kwa makini pindi inapojongea kwenda juu na chini ya mwili wako. Je, kuna maeneo yoyote yaliyokakamaa? Yaliyo na ganzi? Yaliyo na maumivu?
Tulia kwa muda kwenye maeneo hayo kwa muda. Vutia pumzi kwenye eneo hilo na, unaposhusha pumzi, jaribu kuachilia hali yoyote ya kukakamaa au ya maumivu.
Fanya hivi kwa kuvuta pumzi kadhaa.

Fumbua macho yako. Je, mwili wako unahisije sasa?

Unaweza pia kujaribu kufanya hivyo mara ijayo utakapojikuta umelala kitandani lakini usingizi umekupaa!

SourceText: Feel the ground
text: Kuhisi ardhi

SourceText:
Close your eyes.

Notice your connection with the ground beneath you. 
What parts of your body touch the ground? What parts of your body do not?  
Notice where it feels warm and where it feels cool. 
Feel the ground underneath you supporting you. Let your body sink into the support of the ground.

Try this next time you feel alone or are doing a mundane activity like washing up. It can really help!
text:
Fumba macho yako.

Chunguza uhusiano wako na ardhi iliyo chini yako.
Je, ni sehemu gani za mwili wako zinagusa ardhi? Je, ni sehemu gani za mwili wako hazigusi ardhi?
Chunguza mahali palipo na joto na mahali palipo na baridi.
Gusa ardhi iliyo chini yako inayokubeba. Acha mwili wako uzame na kubebwa na ardhi.

Jaribu hivi wakati mwingine unapojisikia mpweke au unafanya shughuli ya kawaida kama kunawa. Inaweza kusaidia kweli!

SourceText: Counting sounds
text: Sauti za kuhesabu

SourceText:
Sit down and close your eyes.
How many sounds can you hear?  
Listen to the sounds inside and outside the room. Count them on your fingers. 
After ten seconds, how many fingers do you have up? What sounds did you hear? 

Try again for another ten seconds.  
Did you hear any new sounds? Did you hear any sounds inside your own body? 
Notice how you feel now.
text:
Kaa chini na ufumbe macho yako.
Je, unaweza kusikia sauti ngapi?
Sikiliza sauti za ndani na nje ya chumba. Zihesabu kwa vidole vyako.
Baada ya sekunde kumi, umefikisha vidole vingapi? Ulisikia sauti zipi?

Jaribu tena kwa sekunde kumi.
Je, umesikia sauti zozote mpya? Je, umesikia sauti zozote ndani ya mwili wako mwenyewe?
Chunguza jinsi unavyohisi sasa.

SourceText: Feel your feelings
text: Hisi hisia zako

SourceText:
Close your eyes.

Do you ever feel something so strongly that you want to run away from it?

Instead of moving away from the feeling, let’s move towards it for a moment.
It is ok. Close your eyes if you feel comfortable. Take a deep breath.

Become curious. Where are you feeling it in your body? Is it hot or cold? Hard or soft? Tight or loose?
Ask yourself some questions. What is it telling me? What does it need? How can I be kind to myself right now?
text:
Fumba macho yako.

Je, huwa unahisi kitu kwa nguvu sana kiasi kwamba huwa unataka kukikimbia?

Badala ya kuikimbia hisia hiyo, hebu tuikimbilie kwa muda.
Si vibaya. Fumba macho yako kama unajisikia raha mustarehe. Vuta pumzi ndefu.

Kuwa mdadisi. Je, unaisikia wapi kwenye mwili wako? Je, ni ya moto au baridi? Je, ni ngumu au laini? Je, imekakamaa au imelegea?
Jiulize maswali kadhaa. Je, inaniambia nini? Je, inahitaji nini? Je, ninawezaje kujitendea wema sasa hivi?

SourceText: Your song
text: Wimbo wako

SourceText:
Here is something fun to help you let go of stress:   

Choose a song that reflects what you need in this moment. Do you need a gentle song to soothe your tired soul or an upbeat song to help you shake some stress out?   

Make a space and move your body to the music. Remember to breathe while you move. Let your breath and the movement go together. 

Even a few minutes of movement can be enough to release stress and lift your mood!
text:
Hapa kuna kitu cha kufurahisha cha kukusaidia kuondokana na msongo wa mawazo:

Chagua wimbo unaoendana na kile unachohitaji kwa sasa. Je, unahitaji wimbo wa taratibu ili kuibembeleza nafsi yako iliyochoka au unahitaji wimbo wa kuchangamsha ili kukusaidia kuondoa msongo wa mawazo kwa kiasi fulani?

Tengeneza nafasi na uchezeshe mwili wako kulingana na muziki. Kumbuka kuvuta pumzi unapocheza. Fanya pumzi yako iendane na miondoko yako.

Hata dakika chache za kucheza  zinaweza kutosha kuondoa msongo wa mawazo na kuinua hali yako!

SourceText: Ground & gratitude
text: Ardhi & shukrani

SourceText:
Close your eyes.

Take a moment to feel the ground under your feet.
Think of something you feel grateful for.
Focus on your breath.
Breathe in and out.

In and out.
text:
Fumba macho yako.

Tumia muda kuhisi ardhi iliyopo chini ya miguu yako.
Fikiria kuhusu jambo unalolishukuru.
Makinikia upumuaji wako.
Vuta pumzi na kuzishusha.

Kuvuta na kushusha.

SourceText: Notice how you feel
text: Chunguza unavyohisi

SourceText:
Hello! How are you feeling right now? Happy, sad, angry, excited, worried?

Notice where you feel it in your body. Notice what thoughts are connected to that feeling. Take a deep breath.

Thank yourself for taking the time to check in with your feelings and thoughts!
text:
Hello! Unajisikiaje sasa hivi? Furaha, huzuni, hasira, taharuki, wasiwasi?

Chunguza mahali unapohisi hali hiyo kwenye mwili wako. Chunguza ni mawazo yapi yanayohusiana na hisia hiyo. Vuta pumzi ndefu.

Hongera kwa kutumia muda ili kuangalia hisia na mawazo yako!

SourceText: Pause power
text: Nguvu ya kutulia

SourceText:
Let’s practice a calming trick that we call ‘Pause Power’.

Plant your feet on the ground and breathe in and out three times as slowly as you can. Imagine you are smelling a flower or blowing out a candle.

Ta-da! Pause Power!

This is a great trick to use when you are feeling frustrated because it will help to calm you down.
text:
Hebu tufanye mazoezi ya mbinu ya kutulia tunayoiita ‘Kata Umeme’.

Weka miguu yako kwenye ardhi halafu vuta pumzi nje na ndani mara tatu polepole kadri uwezavyo. Fikiria kama unanusa maua au unazima mshumaa.

Ta da! Kata Umeme!

Hii ni mbinu nzuri ya kutumia unapohisi kuchanganyikiwa kwa sababu itasaidia kukutuliza.

SourceText: Praise yourself
text: Jisifie

SourceText:
Self-praise can be really helpful, especially when we have difficult days. 

Think of your week and finish the following phrase: “This week, I am proud of myself for …” It can be anything, not just things about being a parent!

Think of one thing you did well today. Now wrap your arms around yourself and give yourself a big HUG!
text:
Kujisifia kunaweza kusaidia sana, hasa kwenye siku zinazotuendea vibaya.

Fikiria jinsi wiki ilivyokuendea halafu umalizie tungo ifuatayo: "Wiki hii, ninajionea fahari kwa…" Kinaweza kuwa kitu chochote, siyo mambo ya malezi tu!

Fikiria jambo moja ulilofanya vizuri leo. Sasa jifumbate kwa mikono yako mwenyewe halafu UJIKUMBATIE kwa nguvu!

SourceText: Taking care of yourself
text: Kujithamini mwenyewe

SourceText:
Sit comfortably and close your eyes. 

Recognise what is happening for you in this moment. What are you thinking? Are your thoughts positive or negative. How do you feel? Do you feel pleasant or unpleasant? How does your body feel? Do you feel tense or relaxed?

Connect to your heart in a kind and gentle way. You may want to place one hand on your heart or chest. Say the following words silently to yourself:

May I be peaceful.
May I be safe.
May I be healthy.
May I be happy.
May there be love in my family.
May I feel loved.

Take a moment to reflect on your experience. Notice if you feel any different.
text:
Kaa vizuri halafu ufumbe macho yako.

Tambua kinachokutokea muda huu. Unafikiria nini? Je, mawazo yako ni chanya au hasi? Je, unahisije? Je, unahisi kufurahi au kutofurahi? Je, mwili wako unahisije? Je, unahisi wasiwasi au umetulia?

Husiana na moyo wako kwa wema na upole. Unaweza kuhitaji kuweka mkono mmoja kwenye moyo wako au kifuani. Sema kimoyomoyo maneno yafuatayo:

Ninaomba niwe na amani.
Ninaomba niwe salama.
Ninaomba niwe na afya.
Ninaomba niwe na furaha.
Na upendo uwe kwenye familia yangu.
Ninaomba nihisi kupendwa.

Chukua muda kutafakari uzoefu wako. Angalia ikiwa unahisi tofauti yoyote.

SourceText: Take a pause
text: Tulia

SourceText:
Step 1. Close your eyes and take a deep breath. 

Step 2. Ask yourself, "What am I thinking?" Notice if your thoughts are positive or negative.
Notice how you are feeling emotionally. Notice if your emotions are pleasant or unpleasant. Remind yourself that whatever you feel, it is okay.
Notice how your body feels. Notice anything that hurts or is tense.

Step 3. Focus on your breath. Feel your breath as it goes in and out. You can put a hand on your stomach and feel it rise and fall with each breath. Do this for about 10 breaths.

Step 4. Expand your awareness to your whole body. Listen to the sounds in the room. 

Step 5. Take a moment to reflect on whether you feel any different. When you are ready, open your eyes.

Well done for taking a pause. You can do this anytime you are feeling stressed. It gives you a chance to be calmer. Even a few deep breaths or connecting with the ground beneath you can make a difference. You can also take a pause with your children!
text:
Hatua ya Kwanza. Fumba macho yako halafu uvute pumzi ndefu.

Hatua ya Pili. Jiulize, "Je, ninafikiria nini?" Chunguza kama mawazo yako ni chanya au hasi.
Angalia jinsi unavyojihisi. Chunguza kama mihemuko yako ni ya kufurahisha au kutofurahisha. Jikumbushe kwamba chochote unachohisi, si kibaya.
Chunguza jinsi mwili wako unavyohisi. Chunguza kitu chochote kinachoumiza au kinacholeta wasiwasi.

Hatua ya Tatu. Makinikia upumuaji wako. Hisi pumzi yako inapoingia na kutoka. Unaweza kuweka mkono kwenye tumbo lako na kuhisi linavyopanda na kushuka kwa kila pumzi. Fanya hivyo kwa mipumuo kama 10.

Hatua ya Nne. Panua ufahamu wako kuhusu mwili wako wote. Sikiliza sauti zilizomo chumbani.

Hatua ya Tano. Tumia muda kutafakari iwapo unahisi mabadiliko au la. Ukimaliza, fumbua macho yako.

Umefanya vizuri kwa kupumzika. Unaweza kufanya hivyo wakati wowote unapohisi msongo wa mawazo. Inakupa nafasi ya kuwa mtulivu. Hata pumzi chache za kina au kuunganishwa na ardhi chini yako kunaweza kuleta mabadiliko. Unaweza pia kuchukua pumziko na watoto wako!

SourceText: Physical activity
text: Shughuli ya kutumia nguvu

SourceText:
Stand up and stretch your arms up to the sky. Push away any clouds and let the sun shine down on you. Stretch to both sides. Stretch to the front and to the back.

Let your hands hang by your side. Squeeze your shoulders tightly up to your ears as you breathe in, scrunch your eyes, and hold your breath. Release your shoulders as you relax your body.

Relax your arms and let them swing sideways while you turn your upper body. Your arms should gently hit your back as you twist from side to side.

Place one foot in front of the other and make small circles from your ankles – remember to turn to both sides. Do each foot with four circles in each direction.

Now shake your whole body as fast as you can. Shake it up high! Shake it down low! Shake it all around!

Close your eyes and raise your arms slowly above your head as you breathe in. Lower your arms slowly to your side as you breathe out.

Take a moment to reflect on your experience.

Well done! You can do this activity at any time whenever you feel like you need to release stress and energise your mind and body.
text:
Simama na unyooshe mikono yako juu angani. Sukuma mawingu yote na uache jua likuangazie. Jinyooshe kwenda kulia na kushoto. Jinyooshe kwenda mbele na nyuma.

Acha mkono yako ining'inie ubavuni mwako. Kaza mabega yako na kuyapandisha hadi kwenye masikio yako huku ukipumua, bana macho yako, na ushikilie pumzi yako. Legeza mabega yako wakati unapolegeza mwili wako.

Legeza mikono yako na uibembeze ubavuni, halafu binua upande wa juu wa kiwiliwili chako. Mikono yako inapaswa kupiga polepole mgongo wako unapojigeuza kutoka upande mmoja hadi mwingine.

Weka mguu mmoja mbele ya mwingine na fanya miduara midogo kwa kutumia vifundo vya miguu - kumbuka kugeukia pande zote mbili. Kila mguu ufanye miduara minne kwa kila upande.

Sasa tikisa mwili wako wote haraka kadri unavyoweza. Tikisa upande wa juu kabisa! Tikisa upande wa chini kabisa! Tikisa mwili wote!

Fumba macho yako na uinue mikono yako polepole kuzidi kichwa chako huku ukivuta pumzi. Teremsha mikono yako polepole kuelekea ubavuni mwako huku ukishusha pumzi.

Tumia muda kutafakari hali uliyoipitia.

Hongera! Unaweza kufanya shughuli hii wakati wowote unapohisi kama unahitaji kutoa msongo wa mawazo na kutia nguvu akili na mwili wako.

SourceText: List of things
text: Orodha ya vitu

SourceText:
Make a list of healthy activities that you like to do. Here are some suggestions:
* Listening to your favourite music
* Going for a walk (if possible)
* Doing some exercise
* Drinking a cup of tea by yourself
* Calling up a friend
* Singing, dancing, praying, or reading
* Sitting in the sun with your eyes closed
* Watching your favourite TV show

Pick one and do it today!
text:
Tengeneza orodha ya shughuli zinazoleta afya unazopenda kufanya. Haya ni baadhi ya mapendekezo:
* Kusikiliza muziki unaoupenda
* Kwenda matembezini (kama inawezekana)
* Kufanya mazoezi
* Kunywa kikombe cha chai peke yako
* Kumpigia rafiki simu
* Kuimba, kucheza, kusali, au kusoma
* Kuketi juani huku umefumba macho
* Kutazama kipindi cha runinga unachokipenda

Chagua shughuli moja na uifanye leo!

SourceText: Connect
text: Unganisha

SourceText: When you take care of yourself, you take care of your children. We all need to connect. Try to talk to friends, family, and other support networks every day. If it has been a while since you reached out to someone, do it now!
text: Unapojitunza wewe mwenyewe, unawatunza watoto wako. Sisi sote tunahitaji kuhusiana. Kila siku, jaribu kuzungumza na marafiki, familia, na mitandao mingine inayosaidia. Kama umepita muda tangu ulipowasiliana na mtu fulani, fanya hivyo sasa!

SourceText: Prevent anger
text: Zuia hasira

SourceText:
Think about what makes you angry. When does it happen? How do you normally react?

Prevent anger from starting in the first place. Get some sleep or rest when you are tired. Try to eat something when you are hungry. Ask someone for support when you are feeling alone.
text:
Jambo linalokukasirisha. Je, linatokea wakati gani? Je, kwa kawaida, mwitikio wako huwa ni upi?

Zuia hasira kabla hata haijapanda. Unapokuwa umechoka, lala usingizi au pumzika. Unapokuwa na njaa, jaribu kula kitu. Unapokuwa mpweke, omba msaada kwa mtu.

SourceText: Angry? Take a break
text: Je, umekasirika? Pumzika

SourceText:
Managing anger can be really difficult. Take a break when you feel you are getting angry at your children or someone else.

Go somewhere else for 5 minutes to regain control of your emotions. If you have a safe outdoor space, go outside. You can get through this!
text:
Kudhibiti hasira kunaweza kuwa kugumu. Pumzika unapohisi unawakasirikia watoto wako au mtu mwingine.

Nenda mahali pengine kwa dakika 5 ili uweze kudhibiti tena hisia zako. Kama una mahali salama nje, nenda nje. Una uwezo wa kulimaliza jambo hili!
